ID: museo-de-la-memoria-y-los-derechos-humanos

Red flags: 2026 cut of the museum's 2027 budget line to 1,000 pesos
- In the 2027 budget debate, the Comisión Especial Mixta de Presupuestos approved amendments that cut the line for the Fundación Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos from 2,642 million pesos to 1,000 pesos. Five other memory sites and programmes were cut to 1,000 pesos each in the same vote (El Desconcierto, Cristian Neira, 11 November 2026).
- The amendments were proposed by the Republican deputies José Carlos Meza, Agustín Romero and Fernando Ugarte during review of the culture ministry's budget (El Desconcierto).
- An open letter to the culture minister, Francisco Undurraga, questioned the cut and answered the argument, which El Desconcierto attributes to government deputies, that the sites "no son de cultura, sino ideológicos": "La barbarie no es un tema ideológico; es la negación de la civilización y la cultura" ("barbarism is not an ideological matter; it is the negation of civilisation and culture", translated) (El Desconcierto).
- Human rights organisations rejected the cuts (El Desconcierto). A column on Radio Universidad de Chile by Patricio López said similar proposals had been made in every November budget debate since 2022, and called on the executive to restore the funds (Radio Universidad de Chile, 16 November 2026).

WIDER CONTEXT
- In 2016 the historian Mauricio Rojas called the museum "un montaje" ("a staged production", translated) and "un uso desvergonzado y mentiroso de una tragedia nacional" ("a shameless and lying use of a national tragedy", translated). La Tercera republished the remarks after President Piñera appointed him Minister of Cultures on 9 August 2018, and he resigned on 13 August 2018, about 90 hours after taking office. The museum's board expressed its displeasure (Emol, 13 August 2018).

SOURCES
- https://eldesconcierto.cl/actualidad/presupuesto-2027-recorta-fondos-sitios-historicos-derechos-humanos-y-deja-1000-al-museo-la-memoria-n5463946

- https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2018/08/13/916826/Rojas-renuncia-al-ministro-de-las-Culturas-90-horas-despues-de-asumir-tras-ola-de-criticas-por-sus-dichos-sobre-el-Museo-de-la-Memoria.html

WIDER CONTEXT
- In 2019 the museum lost its Mali salon gallery at Korzo 24, which it had run for 70 years. The owner of the premises, Croatian Radiotelevision (HRT), notified the museum on 15 June 2019 that it had three months to leave, so that HRT could use the room as a studio for Rijeka 2020, European Capital of Culture. A meeting to ask for more time or shared use brought no agreement (Novi list, 4 September 2019).
- Eighteen museum employees started a petition on Avaaz asking HRT to sign a new lease with the museum in 2021; it had 957 signatures when Novi list reported it. The petition called the removal of the gallery "nepromišljenim činom" ("a thoughtless act", translated). Acting director Ivo Matulić did not sign it and said the museum had already asked HRT for an extension and for the space back after 2020 (Novi list, 4 September 2019).
- The gallery closed with an event titled "Doviđenja, Mali salone!" in September 2019. Speakers at the closing objected to the decision; Janka Vukmir called the return of the space to the broadcaster a symbolic gesture of non-support for culture (Novi list, 13 September 2019).

SOURCES
- https://www.novilist.hr/?p=66772
